pricing.basis: frozen config; the file itself labels it an upper bound for deepseek-chat

S0_s06_basis.assumption: one B+ cell costs exactly one S06 cell; S06 delegated in 0 cells, so this is a lower bound

S1_delegated.assumption: 60% of cells delegate 2 children at 20 turns each; a child turn costs 1200+900x turn prompt tokens

S1b_delegated_6_turns.assumption: the same delegation shape at S06's 6-turn child cap, which no S06 child ever reached because no worker was ever created

S2_budget_fill.assumption: every cell consumes its whole 500 000-token admission budget

nominal_capacity.note: nominal capacity is the admission ceiling, not a forecast. At S06's 93.7 % cache-hit mixture it is cheap; the same tokens with child prompts priced as misses cost what S1 says, which is why S1 and S2 do not order the way their token totals do

dominant_variable.evidence: 20 turns costs 5.6x the 6-turn shape: the child prompt is re-sent every turn and is priced as a cache miss
dominant_variable.decision: S06 requested 6 turns for a profile that caps at 6, so requested and effective agreed. B+ requests 20. The Owner should decide the cap on cost grounds rather than inherit it from a budget sheet

proposed.rationale: covers S1 with margin; S2 is cheaper because it assumes the S06 cache mixture over the whole budget
proposed.canary_shape: one cell per arm on P1, repetition 1, in matrix order
proposed.note: a candidate for the Owner to accept or lower; this module authorizes nothing and no S06 or S08 remainder is carried forward

limitations: S06 measured a no-delegation regime on different tasks; its mixture is an anchor, not a forecast
the child shape is an assumption: no B+ child has ever run, and a 20-turn cap is three times S06's never-exercised 6
child prompt tokens are priced as cache misses because the provider reports no child cache split
the price is the repository's frozen snapshot, not a live quote
whether these cells delegate at all is the largest single cost variable
